summary: netrc credential lookup matched on the full netloc (host:port) instead of hostname alone, letting a malicious/compromised server on an unexpected port receive credentials meant for a different service on the same host.
Proxy URL parsing dropped embedded basic-auth credentials (user:pass@host) when normalizing the URL, silently sending proxy requests unauthenticated instead of failing loudly.

no_proxy domain matching used naive endswith(), so a no_proxy entry like "newdomain.com" would incorrectly also match "evilnewdomain.com" (or "localhost" match "notlocalhost") — a domain-boundary bug with proxy-bypass security implications, ported from a CPython urllib fix.

Authorization header was only stripped on redirect if the hostname changed — same-host-different-port or protocol-downgrade redirects still leaked the Authorization header to a server that shouldn't receive it.

Added specifically to fix CVE-2018-18074 — centralizes the redirect auth-stripping decision (hostname, port, and scheme must all match, with an explicit http->https same-port exception) so rebuild_auth's stripping logic can't drift out of sync with it again.

The connection pool (and its verify=False setting) was cached at the session level on first use; a later request on the same session that explicitly passed verify=True could still silently reuse the unverified pool from the first request.

Uploading a zero-length file-like object set Content-Length: 0 instead of falling back to chunked Transfer-Encoding, because `if length is not None` treated the falsy-but-valid length of 0 as "known" rather than checking truthiness.
